I checked out the food bank when I was in college and made a point of taking some food. I wasn't desperate poor, but I was a regular ol' college-student-without-any-help-from-my-parents poor. I think it's fine for there to be a bit of shame when accepting help, but I think it's important that the shame not be so great that the help is refused by people who really need it. And I think accepting some help when you're only regular poor and not already totally ashamed of your own poverty, might perhaps help remove some of the stigma and shame that is sometimes associated with accepting help when you're desperately poor and already ashamed of being being desperately poor. I certainly wouldn't have taken anything if the food bank was struggling to stay stocked, but if the food bank is stocked well, then I think being willing to accept some help also makes the people running the food bank feel good that their efforts are helping somebody.
